NVIDIA'S CEO HANDED SIX FIGURES TO PLUMBERS
slides.body: Jensen Huang told the World Economic Forum that 'a lot' of six-figure jobs are about to open in plumbing and construction. The reason has nothing to do with houses

slides.headline: AI RUNS ON PIPES AND WIRES
slides.body: Every AI system lives inside a giant building packed with servers, cooling pipes, and wiring. Nvidia wants thousands built from scratch. Someone wins those jobs, but someone else just lost theirs

slides.headline: THE SAME AI GUTTED OFFICE JOBS
slides.body: The same AI creating six-figure trade jobs is quietly deleting the ones behind desks. It writes code, answers emails, files reports. The question now: who adapts first

slides.headline: SMART OWNERS HANDED THE DESK WORK TO AI
slides.body: While everyone argues about jobs, small businesses are using AI to answer every customer in 30 seconds and run scheduling without a single new hire. The ones who moved first are already ahead

slides.headline: THE JOB MARKET JUST SPLIT IN TWO
slides.body: Tool belts or desks. One side is hiring at six figures, the other is shrinking. We track every shift like this. Follow, and send this to whoever still thinks a degree guarantees a paycheck

caption:
Swipe to see why Nvidia's CEO says plumbers will earn six figures from AI, while your desk job is on the other side 🔧

Jensen Huang told the World Economic Forum in Davos that 'a lot' of six-figure jobs in plumbing and construction are about to open, all tied to building the massive AI data centers the world now demands, while the same AI boom quietly threatens white-collar office jobs across corporate America.

The job market is splitting: AI replaces the desk, but it can't lay pipe or pull wire. The trades are becoming the last jobs a machine can't steal, and the AI boom is paying them like it.
